citation: Tully R.B., Courtois H.M., Sorce J.G. 2016, AJ 152, 50

named.name: Large Magellanic Cloud
named.note: A satellite galaxy visible to the naked eye from the southern hemisphere.

named.name: Small Magellanic Cloud
named.note: The LMC's smaller companion, being tidally torn apart.

named.name: Barnard's Galaxy
named.note: An irregular dwarf in the Local Group, sometimes called a miniature Magellanic Cloud.

named.name: Andromeda Galaxy
named.note: The nearest large spiral, approaching us at 110 km/s; it will merge with the Milky Way in about 4.5 billion years.

named.name: M32
named.note: A compact dwarf elliptical orbiting Andromeda, unusually dense for its size.

named.name: Andromeda's satellite M110
named.note: A dwarf elliptical bound to Andromeda.

named.name: Triangulum Galaxy
named.note: Third-largest member of the Local Group and probably a satellite of Andromeda.

named.name: NGC 2403
named.note: An outlying member of the M81 group, rich in star-forming regions.

named.name: Cigar Galaxy
named.note: A starburst galaxy forming stars roughly ten times faster than ours.

named.name: Sculptor Galaxy
named.note: A dusty starburst spiral, the brightest member of the Sculptor Group.

named.name: Bode's Galaxy
named.note: A bright grand-design spiral, gravitationally tangled with the Cigar Galaxy.

named.name: Centaurus A
named.note: The nearest radio galaxy, crossed by a dust lane from a swallowed spiral.

named.name: Southern Pinwheel
named.note: One of the closest and brightest barred spirals.

named.name: Black Eye Galaxy
named.note: A dark dust band across the nucleus, thought to be the debris of a merger.

named.name: Pinwheel Galaxy
named.note: A face-on spiral roughly twice the diameter of the Milky Way.

named.name: M106
named.note: Its distance is known unusually precisely, from water masers orbiting the central black hole.

named.name: Sunflower Galaxy
named.note: Tightly wound flocculent arms rather than clean spiral structure.

named.name: Silver Sliver
named.note: An edge-on spiral with dust filaments rising out of the disc.

named.name: M105
named.note: A classic elliptical, used as a reference for elliptical galaxy structure.

named.name: Sombrero Galaxy
named.note: Seen nearly edge-on, with a dust lane so sharp it looks drawn.

named.name: Deer Lick Galaxy
named.note: A spiral often mistaken for a Milky Way twin, seen with a group of far more distant galaxies behind it.

named.name: M49
named.note: The brightest galaxy in the Virgo Cluster.

named.name: M87
named.note: Home to the first black hole ever imaged, in 2019, at 6.5 billion solar masses.

named.name: Antennae Galaxies
named.note: Two spirals mid-collision, flinging out long tidal tails of stars.

clusters.name: Virgo Cluster
clusters.note: The heart of our supercluster, about 16 Mpc away and pulling the Local Group toward it.

clusters.name: Shapley Supercluster core
clusters.note: The densest concentration of galaxies in the nearby universe.

clusters.name: Coma Cluster
clusters.note: A rich cluster of over a thousand galaxies; the place dark matter was first inferred, by Zwicky in 1933.

clusters.name: Hydra Cluster
clusters.note: A compact nearby cluster dominated by two giant ellipticals.

clusters.name: Centaurus Cluster
clusters.note: The nearest large cluster after Virgo and Fornax.

clusters.name: Abell 2199
clusters.note: Centred on the giant elliptical NGC 6166.

clusters.name: Abell 496
clusters.note: A relaxed, symmetric cluster often used to study intracluster gas.

clusters.name: Ursa Major Group
clusters.note: A loose, spiral-rich group in our supercluster.
